giris.satir: Good tidings, gatekeeper. I am Master Sinan of Ahlat; I have raised caravanserai arches and Horasan-mortared ramparts. When no stone was left standing in the east, I took my plumb line, hammer, and family to this frontier village. If you need a master to unlock the quarry, lime pit, and stone house, let us speak.

secenekler.metin: Your craft is precious, Master Sinan; how much coin do you ask from the village treasury?
Who are the woman and youth by your cart? What shelter do you stipulate?

pazarlik_ucret.satir: My bargain is with the village public treasury, not your personal pouch. To unload my tools and set the quarry, I ask eighteen coins from the village chest. In return, I unlock the secrets of the lime pit, stone house, and second-tier ramparts.

secenekler.metin: I understand the fee; what of your family and housing terms?
We grant the eighteen coins from the village chest and your home; enter, Master Sinan.
Our public treasury cannot bear that cost, Master Sinan; safe travels.

pazarlik_ev_aile.satir: With me are my wife Halime Hatun and my son Davud; we are three souls and need a roof. If your beds are full we can endure the open air briefly, so long as we are not forsaken. My son Davud is now a youth; apprentice him to me at the quarry and in five nights he will be a half-master, then a full master.

secenekler.metin: Your terms are accepted; enter with your family, and let your son train as an apprentice.
We have neither empty beds nor that much coin in the chest; seek another halt.

kabul_sonuc.satir: Your word is your bond, gatekeeper. May our plumb line hang true and our mortar hold fast. Know this from the start: I am a master mason—I do not stand sentry with a spear; my task is to make the wall unbreakable.

ret_sonuc.satir: As you wish, gatekeeper. A wall without lime and arch buckles at the first ram; then you will wish for Sinan of Ahlat.
